input_oneliner: 68M HFrEF EF 30%, admitted for cellulitis, got 3L IVF yesterday, now short of breath overnight, sat 89% on room air

reference_targets_freetext.item: JVP (jugular venous pressure) at 45 degrees, elevated
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Elevated JVP is the strongest bedside sign of elevated filling pressures

reference_targets_freetext.item: S3 gallop (third heart sound) at the apex in left lateral decubitus
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: S3 is highly specific for decompensated heart failure

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea since the fluid bolus
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Orthopnea/PND point to elevated left-sided filling pressures
Positive reflux supports elevated right atrial pressure

reference_targets_freetext.item: Check for new bilateral pitting edema (and sacral edema)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Fluid retention after 3L supports volume overload

should_not_recommend: Empiric IV diuresis before volume examination (JVP, S3 gallop, crackles)
Continuing maintenance IV fluids for the cellulitis without a volume examination
Rely on chest x-ray alone to decide fluid status

perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 68M HFrEF EF 30%, admitted for cellulitis, got 3L IVF yesterday, febrile to 38.9 tonight, now short of breath overnight, sat 89% on room air
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Focal consolidation signs (egophony, bronchial breath sounds, dullness; Focal crackles) become must_have and ask about cough/sputum/rigors rises; JVP and S3 gallop remain must_have; edema check drops to should-still-include.
